mechanisms.name: Leaf certificates (ledger-tls, checkout-tls): default rotationPolicy flips Never -> Always, so every renewal rotates the key
resourcesConsumers: ledger (nginx), which loads /tls/tls.crt and tls.key from a Secret volume
checkout (curl loop), which rereads its files on every call
mechanisms.mechanism: Neither leaf Certificate sets spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy, so both inherit the new default Always. After the upgrade, each renewal (about 20 days after each issuance) produces a new private key where it previously reused the old one. ledger (nginx) reads the cert and key only at start or reload, and no reloader is declared, so it keeps serving its old pair until restarted. That was already true with Never, because the certificate changes on renewal either way. A new key only changes the effect if an old key were revoked or distrusted.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Nothing changes at upgrade time; the policy only applies when an issuance occurs. Kubelet updates the Secret volume atomically, so a cert/key mismatch within one pod is unlikely. Rotating keys is the intended hardening. ECDSA P-256 key generation is cheap, so there is no performance concern. Recommended: set privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly before upgrading. Leaf certificates can move to Always later, once ledger and checkout reload their certificates reliably.
citedEvidence: env/apps/payments/base/ledger-certificate.yaml and env/apps/payments/base/checkout-certificate.yaml set only algorithm (ECDSA) and size, with no spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy
env/platform/cert-manager/values.yaml has no config.featureGates, so DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways stays at its default (enabled in 1.18)
A grep for rotationPolicy and featureGates outside upstream/ and rendered/ finds nothing
rendered/manifest.diff: CRD description changes to "Default is `Always`"; only controller changes are image tags and the acmesolver image arg; no feature-gate arg is rendered
The CRD schema has no server-side default; the default is applied in controller logic, so existing Certificate objects are not mutated and no manifest diff appears for them
Leaf specs: duration 720h, renewBefore 240h (renewal about 20 days after each issuance)

A new key only matters if an old key were revoked or distrusted

mechanisms.name: Root CA (cert-manager/mesh-root-ca): default rotationPolicy flips Never -> Always, so the next renewal creates a new CA key and identity
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: This change newly introduces the failure mode.
resourcesConsumers: ledger (trusts only ca.crt in its own Secret via ledger.conf)
checkout (trusts only ca.crt in its own Secret)
payments mTLS between ledger and checkout
mechanisms.mechanism: At its next renewal (about 11 months after its last issuance) the root CA gets a new key, which means a new CA identity. Previously it kept the same key and subject with a new validity period, so verifiers that trusted the old certificate still validated chains. Both services trust only the ca.crt in their own Secret. A leaf issued after the rotation carries the new CA in ca.crt and is signed by the new key, while a peer still holding a pre-rotation leaf trusts only the old key. ledger and checkout renew independently with no coordination, so between the two renewals one side presents a certificate the other does not trust. The result is mTLS failures: either checkout fails to verify ledger, or ledger rejects checkout, and checkout would log "ledger call failed". The window can last up to about 20 days if the leaf renewals are offset. cert-manager does not re-issue leaves when the issuer CA changes. With a single-CA bundle and no overlap or trust-bundle mechanism, there is no graceful rotation path. Because the root CA renewal is far away, it could surprise someone months after the upgrade.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Nothing breaks at upgrade time; the risk is deferred to the next re-issuance. Mitigation: before upgrading, add privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly to all three Certificates (at minimum the root CA). This keeps today's behaviour exactly and is the documented option 1. Optionally also set config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false as belt-and-braces, but that gate disappears in 1.19 (goes GA), so per-resource Never is the durable choice. Later, design a root CA rotation procedure, e.g. trusting both old and new CA during an overlap, trust-manager, or a coordinated re-issue of ledger and checkout right after the CA rotates.
citedEvidence: env/platform/pki/base/mesh-root-ca.yaml (patched by overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml, which sets only duration, renewBefore and subject) does not set spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy
Root CA prod duration 8760h, renewBefore 720h (renewal about 11 months after issuance)
checkout comment stating it trusts only ca.crt in its own Secret
rendered/manifest.diff: CRD description "Default is `Always`"; no feature-gate arg rendered
The CRD schema has no server-side default; the default is applied in controller logic, so an unchanged manifest hides a runtime behaviour change
assumptions: cert-manager does not trigger leaf re-issuance on issuer CA change (stated by the assessment, not shown as tested)
The repo is the complete declaration of what runs
The assessment says it is unclear whether this failure already existed, but reasons that with Never the root CA key stayed the same, so this change newly introduces the failure mode

mechanisms.name: Not affected: ClusterIssuers, cert-manager install, algorithm/size settings, other Certificates
resourcesConsumers: cert-manager install (CRDs crds.keep: true, single replicas, no prometheus)
any other Certificate resources under env/
mechanisms.mechanism: The rotationPolicy default change could in principle apply to other resources or settings in the environment.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The ClusterIssuers are not Certificates and have no rotationPolicy. The cert-manager install itself is unaffected by this change. Always regenerates keys with the same specified requirements, so algorithm and size are unaffected. No other Certificate resources exist in the repository, and the repo is stated to be the complete declaration of what runs, so there are no hand-applied certificates.

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions. Before upgrading, add privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly to all three Certificates (at minimum the root CA), optionally also setting config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false (removed in 1.19). Then, as a separate change, plan deliberate rotation: leaves move to Always once reloads are reliable, and the root CA gets a rotation procedure first. Missing live-state information and the non-prod tests are listed as needed before proceeding.
overall.quote: Before upgrading, add `privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never` explicitly to all three Certificates (at minimum the root CA).
